title: Proper ample section-algebra reconstruction and polarized naturality
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $f:X\to S$ a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], and $L$ an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] which is relatively ample: $L|_{f^{-1}V}$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] for every affine open $V\subset S$. The graded sheaf algebra $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{m\geq0}f_*L^{\otimes m}$ [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures] is quasi-coherent [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Its degree-zero piece is $f_*\mathcal O_X$, not assumed equal to $\mathcal O_S$. Evaluation defines a canonical isomorphism over $S$
$$r_L:X\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Proj}_S\mathcal A$$
[def-nagata-relative-proj, def-sfb-relative-section-algebra-canonical-map]. On $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$, it is the canonical $R$-scheme map
$$X_V\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Proj}\Gamma_*(X_V,L|_{X_V}),$$
with tensor-product multiplication in the full section ring [def-sc-invertible-section-ring]. For every positive-degree homogeneous section $s$, its inverse image of $D_+(s)$ is the nonvanishing open $(X_V)_s$, and on degree-zero homogeneous localizations it pulls back $t/s^a$ to the quotient of those sections. These maps and their inverses agree on affine refinements of base overlaps. If $f':X'\to S$ is proper, $L'$ relatively ample, $h:X'\xrightarrow{\sim}X$ is over $S$, and $\lambda:h^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}L'$ is an invertible-module isomorphism [def-pc-module-pullback], pullback of sections followed by the tensor powers of $\lambda$ gives a graded $\mathcal O_S$-algebra isomorphism $\Phi:\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal A'$. Its contravariant Proj isomorphism satisfies $\operatorname{Proj}(\Phi)\circ r_{L'}=r_L\circ h$. This equality is compatible with identities and composition of $(h,\lambda)$. No nodality, curve dimension, Noetherian base, finite generation of the full section algebra, or arbitrary-base-change assertion for $f_*L^{\otimes m}$ is required.

source.place: Tags 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample) and 0C6J (lemma-proper-ample-is-proj); constructions.tex Tag 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj) for the graded-isomorphism chart formula. Agent formulation with naturality, extracting former item steps 11--14.

proof.text: Properness gives finite type, hence quasi-compactness, and separatedness; separatedness gives quasi-separatedness. Apply the qcqs section-algebra evaluation theorem to $(f,L)$. Thus $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{m\geq0}f_*L^{\otimes m}$ is quasi-coherent, with its actual tensor multiplication and unit, and agrees with $f_*(\bigoplus_mL^{\otimes m})$. The relative-ampleness criterion applies because $f$ is quasi-compact and the stated hypothesis is precisely its condition (1). Its condition (2) gives $U(\psi)=X$ and the canonical evaluation open immersion $r:X\to P=\operatorname{Proj}_S\mathcal A$. Degree zero in this construction is $f_*L^{\otimes0}=f_*\mathcal O_X$; neither theorem replaces it by $\mathcal O_S$.

Fix an affine $V\subseteq S$ and put $W=f^{-1}V$, $M=L|_W$, $B=\Gamma_*(W,M)$. The qcqs evaluation theorem identifies $\mathcal A(V)$ with $B$, $P|_V$ with $\operatorname{Proj}(B)$ and $r|_W$ with the ordinary canonical map for the identity of $B$. The ample nonvanishing opens cover $W$. The canonical-map theorem therefore gives, for every $s\in B_d$, $d>0$, $(r|_W)^{-1}(D_+(s))=W_s$ and the comorphism $B_{(s)}\to\Gamma(W_s,\mathcal O_W)$, $t/s^a\mapsto t|_{W_s}/s^a|_{W_s}$. In particular these are the tensor section-ring fractions, not fractions in a separately chosen homogeneous coordinate ring.

source.place: Tag 01PZ (lemma-map-into-proj), clause (1); morphisms.tex Tag 01VJ, affine description in the proof of (3) implies (5).

proof.text: The image of $r|_W$ is dense. Indeed $W$ is quasi-compact since $f$ is quasi-compact, and it is quasi-separated since ampleness of $M$ makes $W$ separated, and separated schemes are quasi-separated. Suppose a nonempty basic open $D_+(s)$ misses the image. Step 2 gives $W_s=\varnothing$. The section-ring localization theorem applied to the fraction map in step 2 identifies $B_{(s)}$ with $\Gamma(\varnothing,\mathcal O)=0$. But $D_+(s)=\operatorname{Spec}(B_{(s)})$, so it is empty, a contradiction. The basic opens form a basis, proving density. This proves the density argument of 01Q0 directly from the already stated localization theorem; it is not a new lemma node.

source.place: Tags 01Q0 (lemma-map-into-proj-quasi-compact), density argument, and 01PW (lemma-invert-s-sections), localization; the zero-localization argument replaces the equivalent nilpotence argument.

proof.text: By proper base change, $f_V:W\to V$ is proper. The scheme $\operatorname{Proj}(B)$ is separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$; its structural map $q:\operatorname{Proj}(B)\to V$ is therefore separated by separated cancellation. Since $q\circ(r|_W)=f_V$, proper-over-separated makes $r|_W$ proper, hence its image closed. This closed image is dense by step 3 and so equals the entire target. A surjective open immersion is an isomorphism: its defining identification with an open subscheme now identifies it with the whole scheme. Thus every affine-base restriction of $r$ is an isomorphism.

The evaluation theorem's affine restriction identifications respect all further restrictions. On an affine refinement of $V\cap V'$, both restricted maps are therefore the same canonical map for the restricted section algebra. Their inverses agree as well, since two inverses of the same map are equal. Glue these inverses over the open cover $P|_V$; their two compositions with $r$ are locally identities and hence globally identities. This gives $r_L$. It satisfies the specified canonical-map definition: on an open where $L$ is trivialized, evaluation sends every homogeneous section to its scalar coefficient in the corresponding tensor power of that trivialization. The standard morphism so induced has exactly the inverse-image and fraction formulas in step 2; these determine the same morphism on standard affine charts. This also proves compatibility of both $r_L$ and its inverse on affine refinements of every base overlap, without assuming that an overlap is affine.

source.place: Tag 01VJ, canonical evaluation; constructions.tex Tag 01O9 (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj)(3), affine description; Tag 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), trivialized chart construction.

proof.text: For a polarized isomorphism $(h,\lambda)$ as in the statement, define on every base open the degree-$m$ map $\Phi_m(s)=\lambda^{\otimes m}(h^*s)$, using the canonical comparison $h^*(L^{\otimes m})\simeq(h^*L)^{\otimes m}$. Tensor-pullback compatibility sends $h^*(s\otimes t)$ to $h^*s\otimes h^*t$; consequently $\Phi_{m+n}(st)=\Phi_m(s)\Phi_n(t)$. In degree zero this is the structure-sheaf pullback along $h$, preserving $1$ and the $\mathcal O_S$ action because $h$ lies over $S$. Pullback and $\lambda$ commute with open restrictions, so these maps define a graded algebra sheaf map. It is invertible: pull back by $h^{-1}$ and use the inverse of the isomorphism obtained by pulling back $\lambda$; the composition comparison for section pullback makes both composites the identity in every degree. Thus $\Phi:\mathcal A\simeq\mathcal A'$ is the claimed graded $\mathcal O_S$-algebra isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 01CD (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), 01CT (lemma-constructions-invertible); sheaves.tex, pullback of modules and its composition adjunction. Agent sectionwise tensor calculation.

proof.text: On an affine base open $V$, the local Proj-isomorphism theorem applied to $\Phi$ gives $D_+(s)\mapsto D_+(\Phi(s))$ contravariantly and the comorphism $t/s^a\mapsto\Phi(t)/\Phi(s)^a$. Its affine-restriction compatibility glues these local isomorphisms (and their inverses) to the specified $\operatorname{Proj}(\Phi)$. Pullback of a section along an isomorphism, followed by a line-module isomorphism, preserves its nonvanishing locus, by the fibre formula for invertible pullback: $X'_{\Phi(s)}=h^{-1}(X_s)$. Hence $\operatorname{Proj}(\Phi)\circ r_{L'}$ and $r_L\circ h$ have the same inverse images of all standard opens. Their comorphisms there coincide, since both send $t/s^a$ to $\lambda^{\otimes ad}(h^*t)/(\lambda^{\otimes d}(h^*s))^a$ for $s$ of degree $d$ and $t$ of degree $ad$; this is precisely pullback of the scalar quotient $t/s^a$. These fractions exhaust the chart ring. Equality of the affine chart morphisms, then scheme-morphism gluing, gives the stated global naturality equality.

source.place: Tag 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj), clause (2); Tag 01NQ (relative Proj gluing); modules.tex Tag 01CD and the fibre formula for invertible pullback. Agent comparison of the two fraction formulas.

proof.text: For the identity polarized isomorphism, the section map in step 6 is the identity in each degree; its Proj map fixes every fraction. For a second polarized isomorphism $(k,\mu): (X'',L'')\to(X',L')$, the composite polarization is $\mu\circ k^*\lambda$ after the pullback comparison. On a homogeneous section $s$ the associated map is $\mu^{\otimes m}k^*(\lambda^{\otimes m}h^*s)$, exactly the composition of the two section maps by the composition and tensor formulas for pullback. On a fraction the two successive Proj comorphisms therefore give $\Phi_k\Phi_h(t)/(\Phi_k\Phi_h(s))^a$, the composite section map's fraction. The local Proj uniqueness and gluing identify the two Proj maps, in contravariant order. Substituting the naturality equality of step 7 twice gives the naturality equality for the composite. Identity and composition compatibility follow without choosing any trivializations or identifying the degree-zero algebra with the base.

source.place: Tag 01MZ (lemma-morphism-proj-transitive), specialized to isomorphisms; the displayed fraction and section calculations verify transitivity and the polarization comparison.

tool_uses.why: The generic qcqs evaluation theorem supplies the full graded section algebra and its affine restriction comparisons; this unit has no such general construction theorem.
The generic scheme ampleness criterion supplies the canonical open immersion, without properness or polarized reconstruction; this unit has no such criterion.
The general canonical section-ring map theorem supplies the inverse-image and fraction formulas for an arbitrary invertible module; this unit has no chart theorem.
The generic theorem that an ample invertible module makes its scheme separated supplies the absolute quasi-separatedness hypothesis of section localization; this unit has no such theorem.
The general qcqs section-localization theorem makes an empty nonvanishing locus have zero homogeneous-localization ring; this unit has no localization theorem.
The generic stability of proper scheme morphisms under restriction to an affine base is needed to apply proper-over-separated; this unit has no properness base-change theorem.
The general graded-isomorphism chart theorem supplies canonical Proj maps and restriction compatibility, without line bundles or reconstruction; this unit has no matching chart theorem.
Generic pullback/tensor, section composition and fibre formulas for invertible modules justify the polarized graded map and quotient identity; no node of this unit states these formulas.
